newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar slides on poor export data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar slides on poor export data.

text.p: The release of unexpectedly weak May export data jolted the Singapore dollar's equilibrium on Friday but foreign exchange dealers said it was unlikely to head sharply lower in the near future.

The Singapore dollar slid from around the 1.4250 level against its U.S. counterpart after Singapore's Trade Development Board said non-oil domestic exports fell one percent in May, compared with the same month a year ago.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4272/82 to the U.S. dollar at 0830 GMT.
A Reuters poll of 10 Singapore-based economists on Thursday produced an average forecast of a 3.5 percent year-on-year rise, after April's 5.9 percent rise.
"The market was expecting a plus two to three percent number, but it came out to be minus one percent so dollar/Sing was bought up to a high of 1.4292," a European bank dealer said.
The dealer said the Singapore dollar's downside was capped around 1.4290/95, partly due to caution ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) summit, starting later in the day.
"The market is afraid to short dollars ahead of the G7 meeting this weekend. That's why there's been a lot of short-covering of dollar/mark and dollar/yen," she said.
"I think dollar/Sing should be in a range of 1.4260-1.4290 for the time being," she added.
A Japanese bank dealer said the Singapore dollar could head below 1.4300 next week and possibly test 1.4350 over the course of the month.
"But there's a lot of uncertainty in Thailand still so I think that will give the Sing dollar some support," he added.

Dealers said pressure on the Thai baht after the shock resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Thursday was having a spillover effect on other regional currencies and the relatively solid Singapore dollar stood to benefit.
But Daniel Lian, Asian bond and currency strategist at NatWest Markets, said the regional uncertainty would only be a moderately supportive factor for the Singapore dollar.
"We're not seeing massive attacks on the regional currencies so I think the safe haven the Sing dollar possesses doesn't really support it at this moment," Lian said.
He said the domestic unit was likely to trade a new 1.4280-1.4380 range next week.
"After the bounce in April, everybody thought May would continue to suggest a recovery in exports but...the data cast doubts on whether we're going to see a sustainable recovery," Lian said.
